name: Double junction of conductors
summary: Four conductors joined using two offset T-junctions rather than one crossing dot, to avoid confusion with a crossing.
description: A four-way connection drawn as a cross with a single dot can be misread if the dot is lost in printing or scanning. The double junction draws the same connection as two T-junctions offset a short distance along the line, each with its own dot, so that the connection survives poor reproduction.

Electrically the double junction is the same node as a dotted cross. It does not represent two separate joints. Drafters use it to make the intent robust, and readers should not count it as an additional connection point or a different wire number unless the drawing shows one.
readingNotes: Treat the two offset tees as one electrical node.
Confirm wire numbers are the same on all four branches.
drawingChecklist: Use offset tees instead of dotted crosses for four-way nodes.
Keep the offset small enough to read as one node.
distinction: A double junction is one node drawn as two offset tees; an unconnected crossing has no node at all.
